generated_text: Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m still recovering from Saturday night. That Prosecco was deceptively strong, wasn’t it? Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Tell me about it! I thought I was being sensible with just two glasses, but I woke up feeling like I’d run a marathon. Speaker_1: Poor you. Little Leo's been surprisingly good today though, hasn't he? Sleeping fairly well which is a blessing. You’ve got your hands full with Elsie though, haven’t you? She's a little whirlwind! Speaker_2: She is! Absolutely loves climbing on everything. I’m convinced she’s going to scale the curtains one day. We're thinking about getting that baby gate for the living room. Speaker_1: Good idea. Remember when Mark used to try and climb the bookshelves? Total chaos. Speaker_2: (Laughing) Oh god, yes! He was a menace. Elsie's got the same mischievous glint in her eyes, I swear. Speaking of Mark, are we still on for visiting Mum and Dad next weekend? Speaker_1: Yes, definitely. I booked the train tickets yesterday. Saturday’s probably best, so we can catch the afternoon train home and I can get some proofreading done Sunday. Work's been a bit manic this week. Speaker_2: That’s good you’re getting it in. How's that advertising campaign going for the bakery? Speaker_1: It’s going really well actually! They're really pleased with the social media reach. It’s nice to see that little bit extra coming in. Thinking about Elsie’s birthday… have you got any ideas? She'll be two in February, won't believe it. Speaker_2: I know! Where did the time go. I was thinking maybe a little party at home? Nothing too extravagant. Just a few friends, cake, balloons… Speaker_1: That sounds perfect. We could do a little teddy bear theme? Elsie's obsessed with teddy bears at the moment. Speaker_2: That’s a brilliant idea! I’ll start looking at decorations online. What about a cake? I'm terrible at making cakes. Speaker_1: I’ll do the cake! I’ve been practicing my Victoria sponge. It’s actually quite good now, surprisingly. You can get away with a lot when you're baking for a two-year-old. Speaker_2: (Smiling) True. It doesn’t have to be perfect! Speaking of friends, have you heard from Sarah lately? Speaker_1: Not for a while, no. I'll give her a text. Things have been quiet haven't they. Speaker_2: Yeah. Oh look, Leo's awake. Ready for a feed? Speaker_1: Yep. Want me to hold him while you make some tea? I'm dying for a cuppa. Speaker_2: Yes please, you’re a lifesaver! I'll be right back. And honestly, that Prosecco... I think I need to stick to herbal tea for a while. Speaker_1: (Laughing) Don't we all! A good lesson learned, eh? Between you and me, I think I need to lay off the fancy drinks for a bit. The proofreading's easy going these days, has got to be a blessing. Speaker_2: Well bless you for that! Speaker_1: (To Leo) Hello little man, are you hungry? Yes you are aren’t you. Speaker_2: (Returning with the tea) Right, tea’s here! Now, back to Elsie's birthday… teddy bears, right?H.HH.HH

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m still reeling from how easy it was to hop over to Berlin last month. It really highlights how much we took for granted, doesn't it? Speaker_2: Absolutely. Remember back in the day, the mountains of paperwork just to get a visa for, like, Poland? It felt like a military operation. Book a flight, deal with the consulate, make sure your passport photo was *exactly* the right size… Speaker_1: (Laughs) Oh god, the passport photos! You'd spend longer stressing about the photo than you did actually planning the holiday. I remember Mum nearly having a breakdown trying to get Dad’s to look "official" enough. Speaker_2: And the queuing! I went to Prague in ’03, and the queue at passport control snaked halfway down the airport corridor. You practically needed a survival kit. Now, you just stroll through. Speaker_1: It’s just… liberating. I was chatting to this girl in a cafe in Prenzlauer Berg, and she was from Spain. We were just instantly connecting, you know? No language barriers or complicated visa stuff to navigate first. We ended up sharing recommendations for hidden gem bars. Speaker_2: That’s brilliant. I’ve been looking at flights to Lisbon. Been wanting to go for years, but the hassle always put me off. Now, it’s just... a Tuesday afternoon impulse purchase. Proper easy. Speaker_1: Exactly! I was thinking of doing a few days in Amsterdam at the end of the summer. Research purposes, obviously. Speaker_2: *(Raises an eyebrow)* Research? Into what? The best stroopwafels? Speaker_1: *(Smiling)* Let's just say my work involves understanding consumer behaviour and cultural trends. It's all very valid. Anyway, did you ever manage to figure out that awful French bureaucracy when you were doing your Erasmus in Lyon? Speaker_2: Don't even *start* me on French bureaucracy. It was a masterclass in inefficiency. I swear, they deliberately designed the system to frustrate you. Remember trying to register as a resident? I spent three weeks chasing my tail, got sent from office to office, and eventually just gave up. Speaker_1: Oh, I’ve heard horror stories. Did you at least get to see the sights? Speaker_2: Eventually, yes. It was worth it, honestly. Lyon's amazing. But that registration process... I still have nightmares about it. Paperwork piled up to the ceiling, long queues, people shouting in rapid French... Honestly, it was a test of my sanity. Speaker_1: See, that's what I'm worried about now. Post-Brexit, I’m expecting things to get a bit more complicated again. Speaker_2: I hope not. It would be a real shame to lose that freedom. It's changed the whole dynamic of travel, hasn’t it? Made the world feel a little smaller, a little more accessible. Speaker_1: Definitely. It's made me feel…more connected, somehow. Like I’m part of something bigger. More than just Sunderland and Cambridge, you know? Speaker_2: Aye, you’re right about that. To accessible travel, then. And hopefully, passport photos that don’t look like a mugshot. *raises glass* Speaker_1: *raises glass* Hear, hear! To Lisbon, Amsterdam…and avoiding French paperwork at all costs. speaker_2: Definitely. That’s the plan. Definitely. speaker_1: Good plan. Very good plan indeed. Now, another pint? speaker_2: Definitely another pint. I think we’ve earned it.H.,..

Speaker_1: Right, who wants dessert? I was thinking crumble tonight. Apple or rhubarb? Speaker_2: (Eyes widen) Apple! With custard! Lots of custard! Speaker_3: Rhubarb! Rhubarb is better! It’s pink! Speaker_1: (Laughing) Oh, you two. Alright, alright, we’ll have apple crumble with custard. And a little bit of rhubarb too, just for you, Oscar. Are you two tired of Monopoly yet? Speaker_2: No! Let's play again! I need to win! Speaker_3: I'm gonna buy Park Place this time! That’s my strategy! Park Place and Boardwalk! Speaker_1: That's a very ambitious strategy, Charlie. But those are the most expensive properties. You need some money to actually *buy* them, remember? Speaker_2: I'll lend you some money, Charlie! Speaker_3: Really, Elsie? Thanks! How much? Speaker_1: Elsie, you're meant to be saving your money, not just giving it away! It’s Monopoly, you have to be ruthless! Speaker_2: But it's more fun if everyone has money! And can buy houses! Speaker_3: Yeah! Then we can all build hotels! And charge loads of money! Speaker_1: (Smiling) Alright, alright. But after dessert. We’ll have a think about some rules. Maybe a five-pound penalty for landing on someone else’s property. What do you think? Speaker_2: Five pounds is good! I like that! Speaker_3: Six pounds! Six is better! Speaker_1: (Chuckles) Six pounds? You're getting greedy, aren't you? It's just a game. But, fine. Six pounds. But if you land on my Park Place with a hotel, you're paying the price! How about that, you two? Speaker_2: Deal! Speaker_3: Deal! Park Place is mine! Just you wait! I'm gonna be rich! Speaker_1: (Shaking her head fondly) You two and your dreams of being Monopoly millionaires. Now, who wants to help me peel the apples? Elsie, you can wash them. Charlie, you can pile them up! And please, try not to eat them all before they get into the crumble. Speaker_2: (Giggles) I won't! Promise! Just one. Maybe two. Speaker_3: (Muttering) Park place. Soon to be mine. All mine. Speaker_1: Let's remember to sort the money out properly this time. Last game, Charlie kept sneaking extra ten pound notes out of his pocket! Speaker_3: I didn’t! I just… found them! Behind the sofa! Speaker_1: (Laughing) Right you did. No more 'finding' money behind the sofa. Understand? Speaker_3: Fine. But Park Place is still mine! Speaker_2: You can't find Park Place, Charlie! It's on the board! Speaker_3: (Grumbling) I'll find a way. I always do. Speaker_1: That’s my boy. Now, apples! Let’s get peeling. And then... Monopoly domination! Speaker_2: Yeah! And lots of custard! Speaker_3: And Park Place! And six pounds! Speaker_1: One step at a time, my loves. One step at a time. First, dessert. Then, the ruthless pursuit of property. Then, maybe, just maybe, world domination! One Monopoly board at a time. Speaker_2: I like world domination!H.,H.........

Speaker_1: (Sighs dramatically, leaning her head against the car window) Honestly, this traffic is brutal. I thought coming this way would be quicker, avoiding the A1. Clearly, I was wrong. Speaker_2: (Chuckles, glancing over from the driver's seat) You always think you’ve found a shortcut. Remember that time we tried to get to Gran's in Newcastle via that tiny country lane? Ended up on a farm track. Speaker_1: Don’t remind me! Sheep everywhere. I was convinced we were going to be stuck there forever. Though, to be fair, your navigation skills weren’t exactly stellar that day. Speaker_2: Hey! The sat nav led me astray. It’s not entirely my fault. Besides, it was a good story. At least we got some sheep photos out of it. Speaker_1: Yeah, photos that Mum still uses to tease you about your sense of direction. Speaker_2: (Shakes his head playfully) Alright, alright. But seriously, this is a nightmare. Think we'll make it to Fiona's by six? Speaker_1: Assuming this standstill resolves itself. I’m starving. Did you at least get a pasty before we left? Speaker_2: I did! It’s in the glove compartment. Freshly baked this morning. Best pork and onion you’ll ever taste. Speaker_1: (Brightens up considerably) You are a lifesaver. Honestly, a pasty is all that's keeping me going right now. This commute is proper testing my patience, you know. Especially after that week I’ve had at work. Dealing with all those verbose linguistic ambiguities... Speaker_2: Sounds stressful. Anything specific? Speaker_1: Just… a researcher kept insisting “very” was a meaningful marker of emphasis. Like, just because someone uses "very" a lot, it’s somehow linguistically significant. It’s filler! Pure filler. It means nothing! Speaker_2: (Laughs) Sounds like a proper headache. You and your language stuff. You know, engineering is significantly less philosophical. It’s all cables and stresses and load-bearing capacities. Pretty straightforward, really. Speaker_1: See, that’s what I like about you. You deal in facts. I’m drowning in opinions and interpretations. It’s exhausting. Speaker_2: Well, you're good at it! You’re a brilliant corpus administrator. And you're practically an expert on "very". Speaker_1: (Grinning) Don’t push it. Now, is that pasty going to magically appear, or do I have to threaten you? Speaker_2: (Reaches into the glove compartment) Hold your horses. One pork and onion pasty, coming right up. And maybe a chocolate digestive? You look like you need it. Speaker_1: Don't mind if I do! Thank you. Now, let’s hope this traffic eases up soon. I’m missing Fiona’s lasagna already. Speaker_2: It will. We’ll get there. Just gotta breathe, and enjoy the… ambiance of stationary traffic. Speaker_1: (Dryly) Wonderful. Ambience. Just what I always wanted. Speaker_2: (Smiling) You’re a delight. Absolutely delightful. Speaker_1: The delight is about to get very hungry. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Moving on… any news from your mum? Last I heard, she was planning on exporting her rhubarb crumble to Australia. Speaker_1: (Laughs) Oh, she’s still on about it. Apparently, she’s got a contact who owns a bakery in Perth. Said they're desperate for a good crumble recipe. Speaker_2: (Shaking his head) Only your mum.

Speaker_1: Right then, tea’s on. I’ve put biscuits out this time, not just digestive ones. Got some shortbread and those chocolate things you like, Arthur. Speaker_2: Splendid, Harold. Always good to have a bit of variety, eh? Though you can't beat a good digestive, of course. Good, solid biscuit. Speaker_3: (Entering the room) Oh, that smells lovely. Thank you, Harold. Did you see that article in the paper this morning? About the new bridge they’re building over the Broads? Speaker_1: I did. Looks a bit ambitious, doesn't it? For that location. Lot of water involved. They’ll need to be careful with the foundations. And the wind, of course, those gales can be ferocious. Speaker_2: They always say that, don’t they? “Careful with the foundations.” As if they won’t be! They’re engineers, Harold! Building bridges isn’t exactly a pastime. Speaker_1: I’m not saying they won’t be careful, Arthur. Just that it’s a challenging site. The silt, the tides… they all add complications. Need a good geotechnical survey, that's what they need. Speaker_3: I wonder if they'll disrupt the wildlife. All those birds nesting on the banks. It’s such a lovely spot, usually so peaceful. Speaker_1: They will, unfortunately. There’s always a disruption. But they'll try and mitigate it, I’m sure. Nest boxes, relocation… the usual procedures. It wouldn't be right to just bulldoze everything. Speaker_2: Still, a bridge! Right over the Broads! Seems a bit… unnecessary. I used to enjoy a good row myself. Lovely way to see the country. Speaker_3: Oh, yes. Remember when young Emily used to come with us, Arthur? She'd stand in the bow, pretending to be a pirate. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Aye, she did. Covered in reeds and mud, she was. Happy as Larry. Speaker_1: Speaking of young Emily, has she mentioned anything about her plans for Christmas? Still thinking of coming down from London, I suppose? Speaker_3: I haven’t heard anything definite yet. She did say she was rather busy with work. But she’ll let us know. She always does. Speaker_2: She’s a good girl, Emily. Always was. Got her mother’s good sense, you know. Speaker_1: (Smiling) That she does. Now, who wants another biscuit? I've got a fresh pot of tea brewing too. Speaker_3: Oh, go on then. Just one more chocolate one for me, Harold. Thank you. Speaker_2: Don’t mind if I do. Shortbread’s been lovely. A bit crumbly, mind you. But lovely. Speaker_1: That’s the joy of shortbread, Arthur. Bit of a mess, but worth it. Right, who’s fancy a stroll later? The sun’s out. Would be nice to get some air. Speaker_2: I’m game for a stroll. Bit of fresh air does a body good. Speaker_3: That sounds lovely. But I think I might just sit and read for a bit first. My knees aren’t quite what they used to be. Speaker_1: Suit yourself, dear. We’ll be back later. Just to say we went for a walk. Don't wander off, now. Speaker_3: (Laughing) I’ll try my best! Now, pass me that chocolate biscuit!H...

Speaker_1: So, the sample sizes for the new lavender range are all ready to go. I’ve wrapped them up nicely, little ribbons and everything. Ready for the Instagram photos. Speaker_2: Ooh, lovely! Ribbons are a *must*. Makes it feel more… luxe, doesn’t it? Are you doing a giveaway, then? Speaker_1: I was thinking about it. A giveaway would massively boost engagement. But I’m worried about the cost of postage. It’s bleeding me dry! Speaker_2: Tell me about it. Shipping is the killer, isn’t it? I’m still wrestling with the best way to calculate it on the website. I keep messing up the dimensions. People are expecting free shipping like it’s going out of fashion, the cheek of it! Speaker_1: Honestly! I accidentally put the wrong weight on the last batch of orders. Ended up having to refund nearly a dozen people because I’d overcharged them. Nightmare. Speaker_2: Oh gosh! That's awful. You need to triple-check everything, especially with skincare. People expect transparency. What did you use for measuring? Just a standard kitchen scale? Speaker_1: Yeah, just my kitchen scale. I need to invest in something more accurate. Do you know a good brand? I was looking at those digital postal scales... Speaker_2: I’ve heard good things about those Salter ones. Pretty reliable. And you can get ‘em cheap on Amazon. But, honestly, the customer service calls I had after those refunds… I needed a stiff drink. Speaker_1: (Laughs) I can imagine! Have you considered offering tiered shipping? Like, free over a certain spend? Speaker_2: I’ve been playing with the idea. It might encourage people to add a few extra things to their basket. But I worry it’ll eat into my profit margins. Speaker_1: It’s a gamble, definitely. But building customer loyalty is key. Honesty Skincare is all about building that trust, isn't it? People appreciate knowing where their products are coming from, that they're ethically sourced… Speaker_2: Exactly! That’s the whole point. That's why I’m trying to get the labels printed with the exact percentages of each ingredient. It’s a faff, but… Speaker_1: It’s worth it. That’s what sets you apart! Beauty brands are often so vague. Speaker_2: Speaking of separating out, Mum’s been nagging me to list some of her old earrings on Etsy. Apparently, they’re “vintage treasures.” I'm rolling my eyes, but it could be a bit of extra cash flow. Speaker_1: (Smiling) Oh, your mum's a gem! You should. It's another platform to test the waters, gather ideas. Speaker_2: Yeah, but I don’t want it to distract from Honest Skincare. It’s already taking up all my time! I was thinking of just listing them as “Mum’s Vintage Finds” or something like that. Speaker_1: That’s clever! Separate brand, but under your umbrella. What about holiday plans? Have you booked anything yet? Speaker_2: Not yet! I’m desperately trying to save for a pushchair. Little Leo's getting so big, he has serious leg room requirements now. I was thinking somewhere near the beach next summer, somewhere Leo can run around… Speaker_1: Oh, that sounds lovely! I’m still just dreaming of a week in Italy, a bit of sunshine, pasta… blissful silence! Speaker_2: (Laughing) Blissful silence! A luxury indeed. I'll be lucky if I can get five minutes to myself. So, back to these lavender samples… how many sizes are you offering? And have you worked out the cost per unit yet?

Speaker_1: Honestly, David, the news is just relentless, isn’t it? One thing or another. It's hard to keep up. Did you see about that MP? Absolute disgrace. Speaker_2: Aye, I did. Shocking, really. Thought they’d have learned by now, some of them. The public sees right through it. Though, does it really make a difference, does it? It feels like the same thing happened last month, and the month before. Speaker_1: It’s just disheartening. Makes you wonder what the point of it all is, really. Though, I suppose it’s good to talk about, isn’t it? Better than bottling it all up. How are things with you? Still battling that leaky roof? Speaker_2: Still battling, sadly. The rain's been awful lately. Got a few quotes in, but nobody seems keen to do the job properly. They all say the same thing – "it's a tricky one." Typical. Speaker_1: Oh, I know exactly what you mean. They just want the easy money. You need to find someone with a bit of grit, someone who’s not afraid of a challenge. Did you try that firm, Henderson and Sons? They did a good job on Mrs. Peterson’s place down the road. Speaker_2: Henderson and Sons? I’ll give them a ring, thanks. I'd forgotten about them. They may be a bit more expensive, but it's worth it if they do a proper job. Speaker_1: Absolutely. And how’s Emily doing? Still enjoying her pottery? Speaker_2: She is, actually. She's got a little exhibition planned for next month, down at the little gallery on the seafront. It's all very exciting. She’s nervous, of course, but mostly excited. Speaker_1: Oh, that’s wonderful! I’ll definitely come. I'd love to see her work. I remember when she was little, she always had a creative streak. Making little sculptures out of playdough. Speaker_2: (Laughs) Aye, she always was. And what about you? Keeping busy? Still volunteering at the library? Speaker_1: Yes, still going strong. It keeps me active, you know. And I love being around the books. Got a lovely group of volunteers, we're like a little family. Though, I must admit, I miss teaching sometimes. Just seeing those young faces, their eagerness to learn... Speaker_2: I understand. It’s a rewarding job, teaching. Though, I have to say, some days I wonder why I didn't follow your lead and choose something less stressful. Speaker_1: (Smiling) Nonsense. You were brilliant at it. The kids loved you. You have a gift for explaining things, don’t you? Speaker_2: Well, thank you. That's kind of you to say. So, any interesting books you’ve been reading lately? Anything you’d recommend? Speaker_1: Oh, I just finished "The Song of Achilles." Absolutely beautiful. Heartbreaking, but stunning. You should give it a try. It's right up your street. Speaker_2: I’ll add that to my list. You have good taste, my dear sister. Very good taste. Tell me about your health, are you feeling alright? You seemed a little tired last time we spoke. Speaker_1: Oh, don’t fuss. It’s just a mild arthritis flare-up. Nothing to worry about. The doctor gave me some cream, and it’s slowly getting better. You should have such problems honestly. Speaker_2: Don't be silly, health is important, don't you brush it off....

Speaker_1: Right, so glad you all made it! The stew’s nearly ready, should be bubbling away in about ten. Speaker_2: Smells fantastic, Sarah! Feels good to finally be here, bit of a trek from Newcastle. Snowed over a bit on the way, actually. Speaker_3: Oh, you poor thing, Liam! Luckily Swindon was relatively calm. Though, it *is* freezing, isn’t it? I'm layered up like an onion. Speaker_4: Aye, a bit nippy it is. Though, not as bad as up in Scotland. Had a right blizzard swirling around Carmarthen yesterday. Nearly lost a stack of timber I was trying to dry in the shed. Speaker_1: I’m definitely cranking the thermostat up a notch. It's ridiculous how much energy everything uses these days, isn't it? Thinking about it, I should probably look into getting one of those smart thermostats. Retirement plans, I guess. Speaker_2: Retirement? Sarah, you're barely thirty-five! Speaker_1: (Laughing) I know, I know! Just daydreaming about a time when I can finally grow a proper mulberry tree without worrying about the research budget. Speaking of which, how’s the woodworking going, Rhys? Still churning out those gorgeous bowls? Speaker_4: Aye, keeps me busy. Just finished a commission for a local gallery - a set of nesting bowls using reclaimed walnut. Had to sharpen the chisels something fierce for that one, though. My old set’s starting to go - thinking of investing in some proper Lie-Nielsen tools. Bit of a splurge, but worth it, I reckon. Speaker_3: Lie-Nielsen? Fancy! I'm rather more basic in my recreation activities. I’ve been completely obsessed with Ticket to Ride lately. Have you guys played? Speaker_2: Ticket to Ride? Yeah, I’ve played that a few times. It's a good one, easy to pick up. More my speed than, say, Settlers of Catan. Too much negotiating for me! Speaker_1: I’m terrible at negotiating. I just tend to stress myself out trying to be fair. I'm more of a Scrabble girl, myself. Though my vocabulary hasn't improved much from my research. It's all technical terms and obscure Latin roots. Speaker_3: Speaking of obscure things, did you hear about that new archaeological dig they've started down near Stonehenge? Apparently, they've found evidence of seasonal feasting – loads of pig bones and…mulberries! Speaker_1: Mulberries! That's fascinating! Maybe I'm onto something with that garden plan of mine. Speaker_2: Pig bones and mulberries... ancient Christmas dinner, perhaps? Speaker_3: (Chuckles) Could be! Though, I think they were probably just eating them throughout the year. It's incredible to think how much history is buried just beneath our feet, isn’t it? Speaker_4: Aye, it is. Reminds you that we're just a blink of an eye in the grand scheme of things. Still, a good bowl of stew and a few games sounds like a pretty good blink, eh? Speaker_1: Absolutely! Right, I’ll check on the stew. Anyone fancy a pre-dinner drink? I’ve got some mulled wine…or cider, if you prefer? It's deceptively warming for a cold afternoon. Speaker_2: Mulled wine sounds wonderful, Sarah! Speaker_3: Cider for me, thanks! Speaker_4: Ah, mulled wine for me, then. A bit of warmth would do nicely. Speaker_1: Coming right up!H.H..

Speaker_1: This gravy is absolutely incredible, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Speaker_3: (Warmly) Oh, love, that's good to hear! It's just a bit of Bisto really, but I added a touch of Worcestershire sauce, you see. Makes all the difference. Speaker_2: It’s amazing. Everything's lovely, honestly. Did you manage to find those dessert spoons, Dad? You were saying earlier...? Speaker_4: Ah yes. Right mess, the cutlery drawer. Been meaning to sort it out for ages. Can’t find the dessert spoons anywhere. Seems to be a black hole in there. Speaker_5: (Mumbling from the end of the table) Used to have a whole set, nice silver ones. Belonged to me Granny… Speaker_3: (To Speaker_5) Aye, you did, Dad. Lovely silver spoons. Probably rolled under something years ago. Speaker_1: It's such a classic problem, isn't it? Things just vanishing into drawers. I had that with my scissors at uni. Spent ages looking for them, then found them sticking out from under a pile of socks. Speaker_3: (Chuckles) Oh, you young people! Always losing things. Remember your Auntie Carol? She lost her glasses for three days once, and they were on top of her head the whole time! Speaker_2: (Laughing) Classic Auntie Carol. She's good at that sort of thing. Are you seeing Sarah this week, Liam? Speaker_2: She mentioned she’s got that new exhibition opening she’d love you to go. Speaker_1: No, not yet, I've been swamped at work. And I need to get my flat redecorated... seriously considering a bold colour scheme. Speaker_3: Oh, don't you dare! Keep it neutral, love. You can always add splashes of colour with cushions and pictures. Bold is a nightmare to live with. Speaker_4: Your mother’s right, dear. I tried a lime green bedroom once, years ago. Biggest mistake of my life. Always felt like I was living in a giant lemon. Speaker_1: Okay, okay, point taken. Neutral it is. Although… I was thinking a deep teal. Speaker_5: Teal...like the sea. Nice. Used to sail, you know. When I was a lad. Speaker_3: (To Speaker_5) Remember that trip to the Lake District, Dad? You nearly capsized that little boat. Speaker_5: (Chuckles) Nearly did! Wind got right under me. Scared the bejesus out of your mother. Speaker_2: Speaking of trips, is Uncle David still planning to come down next month? Speaker_3: He's booked his train ticket, apparently. He’s ever so excited to see little Finn. He keeps asking if Finn’s started walking yet. Speaker_1: He has! He took his first proper steps yesterday. It was so cute. We're going to get him some proper walking shoes, he's been wobbling around in those baby ones for weeks. Speaker_4: A good pair of walking boots will do the trick. We have a spare set of safety boots at home. Speaker_3: Oh David's a nostalgic one to change has done for now anyway. Speaker_2: You seemed to have doubled all of your owners size have you any upsets. Speaker_1: That’s quite a lot to be processed. All of those items. Good eating and good having- Speaker_5: Still never sabbath the doors if an important. Trend or something. Speaker_3: Dad you're.H.H..

Speaker_1: So, the meeting went okay then? Did they seem happy with the proposal? Speaker_2: (Mumbles around a mouthful of pasta) Mmmhmm. Happy. Speaker_1: Really? That’s good. I was a little nervous, you know, putting myself forward for that project. It’s a big responsibility. Speaker_2: Big. Like… like mountains, Mummy. Speaker_1: (Chuckles) Exactly like mountains, darling. Which reminds me… Are you excited about the skiing trip? Speaker_2: (Eyes widen) Snow! Lots of snow! Speaker_1: Lots of snow, hopefully. I’ve been looking at the weather reports. Austria looks promising. Speaker_2: Can I build a snowman? A really, really big one? Speaker_1: Of course, you can! The biggest snowman ever. We'll need to find the perfect spot. And snowball fights, naturally. Speaker_2: (Giggles) Can I throw snowballs at Daddy? Speaker_1: You absolutely can. But be gentle, okay? Daddy’s not as nimble as you are. Speaker_2: (Shakes Head) No. Not gentle. Speaker_1: (Laughing) Okay, okay! A little bit gentle. So, I need to confirm the ski hire with that website. And book the ski school for you, obviously. Speaker_2: I want to go fast! Zoom! Speaker_1: You’ll go as fast as you’re ready for, love. We’ll start you on the nursery slopes. Are you practicing your snowplow? Speaker_2: (Puts hands out in a snowplow position) Like this? Speaker_1: Perfect! You’re a natural. Listen, I was thinking, should we get those special ski socks? The really thick ones? Keep your toes warm. Speaker_2: Warm toes! Yes! Speaker_1: Right. I'll add it to the list. It's getting quite long actually. Flights, ski hire, ski school, socks… oh, and we need to get your salopettes checked and adjusted. Are they still too long? Speaker_2: Mmm-hmm. Long. Speaker_1: Right. Speaker_2: (Laughing) Don’t give him ideas, Mum. Bethan, you need to focus. I'm consolidating my position here. Watch. (Places another train) There. Control of the Mediterranean. Speaker_3: (Finally looks up, exasperated) Guys! Can we *please* focus? I’m about to lose everything! The entire Pacific Northwest. Gone! Speaker_4: Speaking of journeys, remember when the trains were always delayed? Used to be the bane of my life. Swear, one time I missed my connecting train to Penang because… Speaker_5: (Interrupting sharply) Dad! No more train stories! Just have a scone. Bethan, are you eating? You look stressed. And Rhys, give her a green train, for goodness sake! You're being a right misery. It’s a holiday, for heavens sake! Have a bit of fun!Huw: (Without looking up) Just need to get to Seattle….

Speaker_1: Right, your turn. Are you going to try and monopolize Baltic again, or are you feeling generous? Speaker_2: (Laughs) Generous? Where would that be coming from? Remember when we used to go to The Dog and Duck in Norwich and just end up chatting to absolute strangers for hours? Speaker_2: Oh god, yes. That was a proper pub. Sticky floors, dodgy lighting, and a landlord who'd tell you his life story if you bought him a pint. Speaker_1: (Laughs) And you ended up playing darts with someone you’d never met before. That’s what I miss. That spontaneity. Speaker_2: Well, you can't recreate that. It's changed. Speaking of games... you know, I was thinking about Settlers of Catan the other day. It's far more interesting than Monopoly, wouldn’t you say? More strategic depth. Speaker_1: It is pretty good. But it takes forever! I always end up getting bogged down in resource trading. It stresses me out. Speaker_2: That’s the fun part! The negotiation, the bartering... It’s a microcosm of life, really. You have to assess who's vulnerable, who's desperate, and exploit it for your own gain. Speaker_1: (Raises an eyebrow) See, there's that capitalist pig again. Speaker_2: (Grinning) It's just observation, darling. Honest observation. Now…are you going to build that hotel on Light Blue or not? Before I unleash my Baltic monopoly upon you? Speaker_1: Fine, fine. But don’t come crying to me when I bankrupt you with my surprisingly lucrative light blue empire.H.HH.HH

Speaker_1: This lentil shepherd’s pie is surprisingly good, isn’t it? Better than I thought it would be. Speaker_2: Yeah, it’s really tasty, Kerrie. You’ve outdone yourself. You’re good with your hands, Kerrie, you’d be brilliant at it. Speaker_2: Yeah, you should give it a go. It's relaxing. Speaker_1: Relaxing is exactly what I need right now. Between the packing, arranging removals, and dealing with the council about bin collections at the new place… It’s relentless! They’re insisting we need two bins, but the plot isn’t big enough. Speaker_3: Oh, good grief, dealing with the council… That’s a special kind of stress. You’ll need to fight for that. Claim you've only got space for one. Speaker_2: Yeah, be persistent. You'll win in the end. Speaker_1: I hope so! Oh, is that Liam banging on the door? Did you bring him along? Speaker_2: Yeah, he wanted to see the new house! Ready to cause havoc? Speaker_3: (Laughing) Oh, I'm sure he is.H.,H..

Speaker_1: This traffic is mental, isn't it? I swear it gets worse every time. Speaker_2: It is dreadful. Should have left earlier. Though, what's the point, really? Would have just been stuck somewhere else. Speaker_1: True. At least we can listen to some music. Fancy some Radiohead? Speaker_2: Oh, please, no. Something a bit…gentler. Speaker_2: Let’s just say I'm considering early retirement and moving to a vineyard in Provence. Speaker_1: Provence sounds good. With lots of sunshine and good wine. Though, I hope you’re being a bit safer behind the wheel. I saw you weave a little bit back there. Nearly gave me a heart attack! Speaker_1: I was just avoiding that maniac in the black van. Seriously, the road rage in London is something else. It's like people forget how to be civilized. Speaker_2: Exactly! It's frightening. And the noise! All that honking… I’m glad we’re going north. The one with the Impressionist paintings. Remember how they were so pleased with the last one? Speaker_1: Yeah, they loved it. Good shout. They're always saying they need more mental stimulation. Speaker_2: They do, don't they? It keeps them going. Speaking of keeping people going, did you ever hear back about that internship with Penguin? Speaker_1: I had an interview yesterday! Speaker_2: Really! Oh, that's fantastic! How did it go? Speaker_1: I think it went pretty well. They seemed really interested in my ideas for their social media strategy. It’s a digital focused role. Speaker_2: That’s brilliant, darling. You’re so good at that stuff. It’s just a shame with print dying out, but it’s the way things are going. Still, there will always be a place for books, even if most people read them on a screen. Speaker_1: I hope so. It just feels…wrong somehow, reading a proper book on a tablet. The smell of the paper, the weight of it in your hand… Speaker_2: I agree. It's a sensory experience. I'll take the smell of old books over a digital download any day. Speaker_1: Exactly! Right, look, there’s a gap in the traffic. I'm taking it! Speaker_2: Careful! And don't weave! I’ll have another heart attack. Just drive normally, for goodness sake.H.HH.HH

Speaker_1: Right, so then the monkey nicked my sunglasses! Honestly, you wouldn’t believe it. Just snatched them right off my face! Speaker_5: (Laughing) A monkey? Where were you, Tarzan? (Everyone groans playfully) Speaker_2: Don't you dare…! You'll traumatize the Yorkshire lass. Speaker_4: Definitely not. I’ve had enough wildlife encounters for one day. Speaker_1: So, you’re actually seriously considering it, Fiona? Wild winter camping? In Scotland? It sounds utterly… bracing. Speaker_2: (Chuckles) Bracing is one word for it, David. Challenging is another. But aye, I've been reading up on it, and the photography potential alone is incredible. Imagine, snow-dusted landscapes, the Northern Lights… Speaker_3: It's not just photography, Mum. There's something really primal about it. Stripping back to the basics, being completely reliant on your own skills and the environment. I’ve been looking into it too, actually. Speaker_1: You are? Hamish, I didn't realise you had the inclination for such a... rugged pursuit. You always struck me as the literary type, buried in books. Speaker_3: Well, I appreciate a good book, but I've been feeling the need to reconnect with nature lately. All this data and strategy and curriculum development... it gets a bit detached, doesn't it? And a lot of younger people are embracing these sorts of experiences. Speaker_2: Exactly. It’s about resilience, and appreciating the simple things. It's a very different kind of therapy than what I offer in the office, you know? A really deep, visceral kind. Speaker_1: I can appreciate that. Though the thought of being exposed to the elements like that... It sounds terribly uncomfortable. What about hypothermia? What about the midges, even in winter? Speaker_3: Midge season is over, Dad. Mid-December onwards they're practically non-existent. And hypothermia is manageable with proper gear and preparation. It's about understanding the risks and mitigating them. I’m thinking a four-season tent, good layering system, thermal sleeping bag… Speaker_2: I’ve been looking at Exped tents - they're surprisingly spacious for their weight. And I’m taking a wilderness first aid course in January, just in case. No need to be reckless, David. Speaker_1: Wilderness first aid, eh? Sounds like you’re planning for the worst. What about food? Are you going to be foraging or...? Speaker_3: Dehydrated meals mostly, Dad. Lightweight and easy to prepare. And I'm learning some basic wild edibles - there are still some berries and mushrooms that can be found even in winter, though you have to be *extremely* careful. Speaker_2: I have a friend who’s a botanist. I’ll ask her for a list of safe and reliable ones. It’s fantastic getting to learn that side of things too - acknowledging what nature provides and learning to respect it. Speaker_1: I still maintain it sounds freezing. But I suppose there’s something admirable about embracing that level of… self-sufficiency. You know, my father used to go fishing on the Thames, in all weathers. He wouldn’t have complained about the cold. Speaker_3: It’s not just about enduring the cold, Dad. It's about appreciating the stillness, the silence. You’ll notice things you wouldn't otherwise. The patterns in the snow... the way the light plays on the frost... Speaker_2: You’ll find a whole new kind of peace, David. A different perspective. And I’ll take lots of photos of the Northern Lights to show you when I’m back. Speaker_1: Well… if you're going to do it… at least be careful. And tell someone where you’re going. And take a flask of tea – a *good* flask of tea. That’s essential. Speaker_3: Of course, Dad. Wouldn’t dream of going without the tea.H...

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m still buzzing from that film. "Everything Everywhere All At Once," right? It's just… a lot. Speaker_2: It was intense, yeah. Visually stunning, though. And the acting was phenomenal. Michelle Yeoh was incredible. Speaker_1: Incredible doesn't even cover it. The sheer range she had to display, jumping between universes, different personalities… It was mental. I kept thinking about that bagel scene, though. Just… wow. Speaking of appreciating things… I had this absolutely unbelievable curry last night. A little place down the road, “Spice King,” you’ve never heard of it. Speaker_2: No, haven’t. Is it good? You wouldn't regret it. Although, fair warning, the décor is… well, let's just say it wouldn't win any design awards. Speaker_2: As long as the food is good, I'm not bothered about the décor. I’ve been reading this fascinating essay about the use of language in… it’s a bit dense to be honest. Speaker_1: Oh yeah? What’s it about? I always fancy a good read. I finally got around to "Frankenstein" last month. Speaker_2: It’s about the semiotics of online communication. It's like a whole other layer of meaning. Do you think it blurs the lines between genuine emotion and just… performance? Speaker_2: That’s what the essay argues. It’s really interesting, but it also makes you think a bit differently about how we use language, both online and offline. It’s made me feel a bit cynical, actually. Speaker_1: Well, a bit of cynicism never hurt anyone. Just don't let the bagel take over. We need to hold onto the good stuff, remember? Speaker_2: Absolutely. Spice King it is, then? We can discuss the decay of modern language over Rogan Josh. Speaker_1: Deal. And I'll make sure they put extra coriander on mine. You deserve it. Speaker_2: Haha – Thanks. Good plan. Let's just try and avoid any sudden universe-hopping whilst we’re there. Speaker_1: Agreed.H.H..

Speaker_1: Right, story time! Are you both snuggled in? Speaker_2: (Giggles) Yes, Mummy! Can we have the one about the very hungry caterpillar? Speaker_3: No! The one with the dragon! It feels like only yesterday they were little ones, clinging to my legs. Speaker_2: Time flies, doesn’t it? It's the same with my lot. The eldest is practically an adult now. Speaker_1: Right, so I’ve ordered the salmon, and I’m thinking a lemon and dill sauce? What do you reckon, Dave? Speaker_2: Sounds lovely, love. Salmon’s always a winner. You getting any veg with it? Speaker_1: Yes, broccoli and some of those little new potatoes. And I’ve got that new cider from Waitrose, the one you liked. Speaker_3: Ooh, exciting! Can I have extra potatoes, please? Less Deliveroo, more… actual cooking. Speaker_2: Good for you, sweetheart. Better than spending all your time glued to that mobile phone. Facebook’s a rabbit hole, you know. They’re a force of nature. Did you tell her about that new body scrub you bought? The one with the sea salt? Speaker_1: I did! She said it would be ‘far too abrasive’ for her delicate skin. As if she’s not 83! Speaker_2: She just likes to moan, doesn't she? Remember last Christmas when she said the turkey was too dry, and then devoured three helpings? Speaker_3: (Laughing) Classic Mum. So, any plans for New Year’s then? Speaker_1: We were thinking of just staying in, really. Order some Chinese, watch a film. Low key. Speaker_2: Sounds alright to me. Less stressful than going out. Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m still reeling from that documentary on the energy crisis. It’s just… relentless. Everything’s going up, isn't it? Speaker_2: Tell me about it. Though, in retrospect, it was pretty obvious, wasn't it? Speaker_2: Maybe a little. Still, the atmosphere was incredible. Anyway, enough about dystopian office dramas. How's the copywriting going? Speaker_2: That’s great though! Sounds really interesting. Way better than toilet cleaner. Got any big plans after uni? Aside from, you know, saving the planet via copy? Speaker_1: It’s terrifying. It's hard to imagine leaving London, but it's also… exhausting. How's your mum doing? Still going on about you getting a "proper" job? Speaker_2: (Rolling her eyes) Constantly. Mine's still trying to convince me to join the police force. Says it’s got “pension stability.” Speaker_2: Pension stability! That's the metric for a fulfilling career now? Speaker_1: Apparently. So, are you seeing anyone? Still dating that guy from the library? Speaker_2: Nope! He was… intensely enthusiastic about medieval history. A little too intense, for my liking. I’m focused on finishing my dissertation now, really. Until I die, basically. Speaker_1: Fair enough. Well, you should put yourself out there when you're done. We’ll need to have a girls’ night and dissect all the dating disasters. Speaker_2: Deal. Actually, speaking of girls' nights, are you free next weekend? Chloe's organizing something… a karaoke night in Shoreditch. Speaker_1: Karaoke? Shoreditch? You know I can’t sing. Speaker_2: Nobody cares! It'll be a laugh. Come on, you need to let loose a little. Speaker_1: Hmm… Okay, okay, you’ve twisted my arm. Just promise you'll film me so I can cringe about it later.

Speaker_1: Honestly, I’m feeling it today. My back is protesting every single step I take. Speaker_2: You’ve been doing too much Pilates, haven't you? Trying to be a twenty-year-old again. Speaker_1: Don't you start. I need to stay active, you know. Otherwise, I'll just be a lump on the sofa, watching documentaries about obscure fungi. Speaker_3: You’d enjoy the fungi documentaries. It's not as easy as it used to be. Speaker_1: True, but I’d rather commute than spend all my savings on a tiny box with peeling wallpaper. Have you been trying out any new recipes lately? Something to take your mind off the housing crisis? Speaker_3: (Smiling) I did make a rather lovely lemon and thyme chicken the other day. It was surprisingly easy, actually. I found the recipe online. Speaker_1: Lemon and thyme? Sounds delicious. I’ll have to try that. I’ve been attempting a Moroccan tagine… with very mixed results. Speaker_1: You’re right, you're right. I’m being too timid. Maybe I'll just stick to the lemon and thyme chicken for now. It can't be that hard, can it? Speaker_3: Not at all. Honestly. I'll text you the recipe. And maybe you could try a little Pilates, but gently! Speaker_1: (Groaning playfully) Don't push your luck.H.H..

Speaker_1: Honestly, the new corpus interface is driving me absolutely mental. They’ve completely changed the search functionality. Speaker_2: Oh, really? Still wrestling with that, then? I remember you were pretty stressed about the changes last time we spoke. Speaker_1: Stressed is an understatement. It’s like they’ve actively tried to make it more difficult for users. So, anything exciting happening outside of bridges and stress calculations? I know you were talking about seeing a musical? Speaker_2: Yeah! I managed to get tickets for *Wicked* next month. You free? Fancy coming with? Speaker_1: *Wicked*! Oh, I’d love to! I’ve heard it's amazing. Been ages since I’ve seen a good musical. Speaker_2: Me too. It’ll be a nice change from blueprints and concrete! Speaker_1: Definitely. When are you thinking? It's just so lovely here today; it's nice to be around greenery for once. Speaker_2: Let me check my calendar… Actually, how about the evening of the 17th? Should be a Saturday. Speaker_1: The 17th sounds perfect. Let me just double-check my diary, but I think I'm clear. Send me the details. I’m definitely in. Speaker_2: Sorted! I’ll forward the booking confirmation over. Glad you could make it. It'll be great to catch up outside of emails and instant messenger. Speaker_1: Absolutely! It's good to get some face-to-face time. Plus, I desperately need a distraction from the corpus chaos. Speaker_2: Fair enough. Sounds like you need that *Wicked* magic! Speaker_1: I certainly do. Right, well, I’ll let you get back to basking in the sunshine. You look like you’re enjoying that. Speaker_2: Definitely. Taking it all in. Cheers! Speaker_1: You too! Bye! Speaker_2: Bye! Goodbye. Speaker_1: Bye! Bye! Speaker_2: Goodbye.H.,H..

Speaker_1: Right, so I’m thinking a kind of muted grey for this section of the fence, blends in a bit more, don't you think? Less jarring against the brick. Speaker_2: Mmm, grey's alright. Bit dull though, innit? Shoulda gone for a brighter colour, like. Give it a bit of character. Speaker_1: Character, yes, but I’m trying for something a bit more… subtle. Something that doesn't shout. I'm more comfortable behind the scenes these days, you know, with the language, the literature... analyzing it. Speaker_2: Speaking of things behind the scenes, they’re starting to tear down them old warehouses down by the docks, aren't they? Speaker_1: Yes, another block of flats, I suppose. More luxury apartments for people who don’t need ‘em. It’s depressing, really. What are they doing to Liverpool? Speaker_2: Progress, they call it. Got yer politicians spinning stories, don't they? Used to be a lot of character down there. Proper artists, craftspeople. Now it’s all chain shops. Speaker_1: Exactly. It’s a shame. I picked up a lovely old watercolour down at a car boot sale last week – landscape of the docks, from the 50s, it must be. Speaker_2: Ooh, show me that sometime. I’m always looking for a bargain. Speaking of bargains, you still need that ladder to get up to the gutters? Speaker_1: Yes, actually. Those gutters are a nightmare. Keeps leaking. I’ve been meaning to sort them out for weeks. Speaker_2: I’ve got one in the garage. A bit wobbly, mind, but it’ll do the job. You can borrow it. Just give it back when you’re done. Speaker_1: Brilliant! Thank you, Dave. Really appreciate that. I'll bring you a couple of beers as a thank you. Speaker_2: Cheers, that’s grand. I'm always needing a reason to crack open a cold one. You know, I was thinking of getting myself a little easel and trying to learn to paint myself. Speaker_1: Really? That’s lovely, Dave! You’d surprise yourself. You’ve got a good eye. Speaker_2: Just messing about, like. Probably end up painting a picture of a taxi cab. Speaker_1: (Laughs) That would be wonderfully Liverpudlian! So, grey or no grey? Speaker_2: Grey’s alright, I suppose. But if you change your mind, I got a can of bright orange in the shed… might cheer the place up a bit. Speaker_1: (Smiling) We’ll see. We’ll see. Let’s finish this section first, eh? And then, perhaps, we'll talk about that orange. Speaker_2: Sound. You want another cuppa? I'll pop inside.H...

Speaker_1: (Looking out the window) Oh, look, more fields. Just...fields. It's quite monotonous, isn’t it? Though the light is rather lovely on them this afternoon. All golden-y. Speaker_2: Yeah, it is a bit. Still, beats staring at a classroom wall, eh? At least we’re *seeing* something. And it's miles better than Bury, honestly. Not that I'm knocking Bury, it's just... this is different. Speaker_1: Absolutely. Though, I am starting to miss having a proper cuppa. That instant stuff just isn't the same. Did you manage to track down any decent Polish biscuits? Speaker_2: I got some yesterday in Zakopane, the kind with the poppy seeds. They were actually all right. We should stop at a shop soon, I’m starting to feel peckish. Are we still on track for Tarnów by, like, seven? Speaker_1: I think so. Google Maps is being fairly cooperative. Although, honestly, driving through Poland is just...it’s a palate cleanser after years of just saving up and then sorting through boxes. You know? Speaker_2: Yeah, I get it. So much stuff. You're really making progress clearing out the flat, aren't you? Mum seemed really pleased when I spoke to her. Speaker_1: It's liberating, actually. I’m selling bits online. Someone bought that ridiculous ceramic frog I'd had since university! Can you believe it? Speaker_2: Seriously? That thing was hideous! Good riddance. You should’ve been posting those pictures of everything you’re selling, I’d have bought a few things for my flat. Speaker_1: I will, I promise. Right now I’m just focused on getting rid. It’s quite a strange feeling, letting go of things you've held onto for decades. Speaker_2: It is. I think that’s why I'm finding this trip so good. A total reset. Remember that time we tried to hitchhike to Whitby? Speaker_1: (Laughing) Oh god, yes! That was a disaster. We ended up stranded in some tiny village and had to beg a farmer for a lift. Speaker_2: And he smelled strongly of sheep! Still, it's a good story. Makes you appreciate having a campervan with a working toilet, doesn't it? Speaker_1: It certainly does! Have you heard from Liam recently? I’ve been meaning to message him. Speaker_2: Yeah, he's in Berlin, apparently. Said he's loving it. Properly living the expat life. Bit jealous, not gonna lie. Speaker_1: So are you still planning on going to that festival in Manchester when you get back? With Sarah and Chloe? Speaker_2: Definitely. Gotta see them. It’s nice to have some familiarity when you’re bouncing around Europe. And I owe Sarah a ridiculous amount of Prosecco after she helped me move all those boxes. Speaker_1: You always do! Speaking of boxes… I’ve got another one to sort through when I get back. A suitcase full of old photographs…that’s going to be a weekend project. Speaker_2: Oh crikey. Well, at least you've got some fuel for your next philosophical unpacking session. And we'll have another trip before then, yeah? Somewhere…sunnier. Speaker_1: Absolutely. Somewhere with less fields. And definitely better tea. Maybe Italy? Speaker_2: Italy sounds amazing! Alright, let’s aim for that then. Just gotta get to Tarnów first. I'm seeing a weird sign. Looks like a badger wearing a hat. Speaker_1: (Laughing) You’re making that up. Polish road signs are not that quirky. Focus on the driving, love!

Speaker_1: Are we nearly there yet? My legs are aching. Speaker_2: Almost, love. Just another ten minutes or so. You alright? You seem a bit tired. Speaker_1: Yeah, I stayed up late reading. I’m halfway through ‘The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida’ – it’s brilliant, Dad, you should read it! Speaker_3: Ah, I’ve heard of that. Sheku recommended it, didn’t he? Bit heavy going though, isn’t it? All that political stuff. Speaker_1: It’s intense, yeah, but the writing’s really clever. And it's got this really weird afterlife storyline, which is quite morbid but fascinating. You know like… people just hanging out waiting to be reborn. Speaker_2: Sounds a bit grim for a car journey, doesn’t it? Speaker_1: Not really, it makes you think. Remember when you wanted me to go to the Hay Festival? Speaker_2: Yes! And you didn't want to. I still think you should go. All those authors... Speaker_3: Hay Festival’s brilliant. Shame I missed it last year, completely wiped out with that chest infection. Thought I was going to end up in hospital. Speaker_1: Speaking of things wiping you out, how are gran and grandad? Did you call them today? Speaker_2: I did ring them. Gran’s saying she's feeling a bit better, but still struggling to sleep. Doctor thinks it might be those new pills they gave her. Speaker_3: Those pills they give people these days! They never tell ya the side effects. It's a racket, it is. I remember my mum took something off the telly once for her arthritis... ended up with blisters all over her feet! Speaker_1: Seriously, Dad? Speaker_3: I'm serious! Right as rain one minute, walking around like she’d been through a furnace the next! Should've stuck to Epsom salts, that's what my grandma always used to say. Speaker_2: What are we getting from Preston today, anyway? Besides cheering you up. Speaker_1: We need milk, bread and some chocolate. And I wanted to go into Boots to get… oh, I can’t remember! Something for exams. Speaker_3: Exams already? You’re flying through school. It's only just started. Speaker_1: Yeah, but they’re looming, aren’t they? Plus, you know, that move is stressing me out. I need to de-stress somehow. Actually, I think I'll check online for some relaxation spotify playlists. Speaker_2: Don't forget we need some new towels for the bathroom. The ones we have are looking a bit threadbare. Speaker_3: Threadbare! Fancy that. You’d think after all these years, we’d have thrown them out. They used to be lovely thick ones you know, from that shop in Bolton. Remember, Doreen's Emporium? Speaker_1: No, Dad. You’re talking ancient history. Speaker_3: Ancient history? It was just before you were born! They had the best towelling dressing gowns too. Wonderful quality. Not like the rubbish you get these days. Speaker_2: Don’t start, David. Don’t get us reminiscing about everything that was better in the old days. We'll be stuck here all day. Speaker_1: Oh, look! Preston’s coming up! At least we're nearly there… Ugh, I really hope the train strikes haven’t caused too much chaos. I need to get back for study group. Speaker_2: Don't you worry. I’ll check the updates as we go.

Speaker_2: Nan! What are you doing here? This is brilliant! Didn’t expect to see you for ages. Speaker_1: (Chuckles) Well, I thought I’d surprise you all. Your son – my grandson – said you were all here, in Thirsk. And I thought, "Right, I’ll pop up!" Speaker_3: Nan! You're here! Wow. You look…well, you look like Nan! Speaker_1: (Smiling warmly) And you’ve grown another inch, haven’t you, lad? Last time I saw you, you were still struggling to reach the biscuit tin. Needed a bit of a change. And I wanted to see your face, love. It's been too long since I've seen you properly. Besides, I was sorting through some old boxes back home and found a hilarious sketch from that comedy club we went to years ago. Reminded me of you. Speaker_2: Oh, you haven’t! The one with the pigeon? Seriously? I’d forgotten all about that. Speaker_1: (Chuckles) And you were nearly choking with laughter! You sprayed your drink everywhere, didn’t you? Speaker_3: A pigeon sketch? Was it good? Speaker_2: It was brilliant, love. Really silly. Nan's got a good eye for funny. She used to drag us to all sorts of open mic nights. Speaker_1: Well, you children need a bit of silly in your lives! Though I must say, all this technology you youngsters have now… it’s baffling. I tried to send an email the other day, and I ended up ordering five gardening gnomes online. Speaker_2: (Laughing) Oh, Nan! Don't tell me! Speaker_1: It’s true! I was trying to find Susan’s address, and I got completely lost. These icons… and the drop-down menus… utterly confusing. Speaker_3: It’s easy once you get used to it, Nan. I can show you. Actually, I've been learning loads about coding. It's pretty cool. Speaker_1: Coding? What's that? Sounds like something you do in a spy movie. Speaker_2: He’s learning to write computer programs, Nan. Basically, telling the computer what to do. Speaker_1: Fancy that. Well, you’re a clever lad. I'm proud of you. But tell me, are you two clearing out that garage like you said? It’s been months now. Speaker_2: We’re trying! It’s a monumental task. It’s full of… well, everything. Your old china cabinet is in there, remember? And your collection of thimbles. Speaker_1: Oh, my thimbles! I’d love to see them again. Perhaps I could have a look when I'm here. Speaker_2: Definitely, Nan. We’ll make some time. It’s just…heavy going. It’s stirred up a few memories, some a bit sad to be honest. Uncle George’s things… it's been hard. Speaker_1: (Her voice softens) I know, dear. It never gets easier, does it? Those memories are precious, though. It's important to remember the good times, even when it hurts a little. And if you're struggling, talk about it. Don’t bottle things up. Speaker_3: It’s alright, Nan. We’re managing. Mental health stuff is getting easier to talk about these days, you know? Speaker_1: That’s wonderful to hear. It shouldn't be a taboo. Good for you, both of you. Now, I’m famished! What are we having for dinner?

Speaker_1: Right, so, initial impressions? What do you reckon of the new machine? Speaker_2: It’s… surprisingly nippy, isn’t it? Loads better than yours was, for sure. Let's see if it can handle it without melting down. Speaker_2: Right, let's fire it up. Got Premiere Pro installed, yeah? Speaker_1: Yep, all sorted. Tried a quick render earlier, seemed pretty promising. What about you, Alex? Still beating people up at the gym? Speaker_3: Nah, not this week. Got a dodgy knee. Trying to be a bit kinder to myself, you know? Maybe take up line dancing instead. Speaker_1: Line dancing? Seriously? Speaker_3: Don't knock it till you’ve tried it! All those repetitive movements are good for the core, apparently. Plus, the ladies seem to enjoy it. Speaker_2: You’re a menace, Alex. Anyway, this video's loading… yeah, it’s actually surprisingly quick. Considering it’s 4K. Speaker_1: That’s a relief. The old one would have taken forever. Remember that project I did for that wedding? Took a whole weekend just to render. Speaker_2: Oh god, the one with the disastrous cake cutting? Still makes me laugh. Speaker_3: Speaking of disasters, did you see that article in the Bedfordshire Gazette about Mrs. Higgins' cat getting stuck in a tree again? Speaker_1: No, what? Really? That's the third time this year! Speaker_2: Poor kitty. Someone really needs to get that cat a harness. Speaker_1: You're right. Where have you been getting your groceries from latel. Speaker_2: The new Korean place. They have amazing kimchi. Seriously, best I’ve had outside of Seoul. Speaker_3: Korean food, eh? I've not really ventured past the usual. You gotta tell me what to order. Speaker_1: Yeah, recommend something, man. I’m trying to eat a bit healthier, you know? Less beige food. Speaker_2: Get the Bibimbap. Loads of veg, good protein, and it's got that lovely spicy kick. Speaker_3: Right, noted. I might have to give that a go. What about this new TV you were looking at? The one with the crazy refresh rate. Speaker_1: Oh yeah, the OLED. It's tempting, but pricey. Waiting for the price to drop a bit, you know? Besides, I’m happy enough with what I’ve got for now. After this render, I'm going to try and install that retro gaming emulator I was talking about. Speaker_2: Oh, you're going down memory lane, are you? What are you planning on playing first, Pac-Man? I’m more of a FIFA man myself, but hey, to each their own. Speaker_1: You've got to appreciate the classics. Plus, the graphics still look pretty good on this new screen. Have a look at the sound settings. I think they've messed something up.

Speaker_1: This place is lovely, isn't it? I mean, Tarnów wasn’t exactly overflowing with trendy bistros last time I was here. Speaker_2: It’s really good! The decor's so… Scandi-chic. And their coffee's proper good. I wasn’t expecting that in Tarnów, to be honest. Speaker_1: No, me neither. I’m impressed. Though, the prices are a bit steep, aren't they? More London prices than anything I'd expect here. Speaker_2: Yeah, a little pricey, but hey, it’s nice to treat yourself sometimes. Speaking of treating yourself, have you been to the new Primark that opened up? Speaker_1: Not yet! Been a bit too busy trying to sort out my TEFL students. It’s a minefield, honestly. One wants to learn only about football, one is obsessed with American sitcoms... Speaker_2: Tell me about it! Trying to keep them engaged when their English isn’t exactly fluent is… challenging. But rewarding, you know? Seeing them progress is brilliant. Speaker_1: Absolutely. Reminds me of why I did it in the first place. Though, I do miss having a bit more… control over my own time, if I'm honest. This freelance thing is exhausting. Speaker_2: It’s always going to be. It’s hard being your own boss. But the flexibility is awesome. Remember when we were younger and dreamt of being completely independent? Speaker_1: (Laughs) Oh, God, yes. We were so idealistic. Do you ever think about that stuff now? Like, are we even close to what we thought we'd be? Speaker_2: Sometimes. I mean, I have a job I enjoy, I’m living abroad… That’s a pretty big tick in the ‘life goals’ box, isn't it? Though, I do sometimes wonder about settling down and having a family. Speaker_1: It's a big decision. And a scary one. You know, it’s funny, my sister was saying how she’s struggling with… well, it's a bit of a long story, but it involves a bit of an addiction problem with her partner. Speaker_2: Wow, that’s awful. Is she okay? Speaker_1: She’s trying. It's tough. You know, I always thought I'd have it all sorted by now, but life threw a few curveballs, didn’t it? Keeps you wondering who you really are, doesn’t it? Like, are you defined by your choices, or by your circumstances? Speaker_2: Deep thoughts over coffee! I know what you mean. It's like you can spend ages trying to craft the perfect identity. But the thing is, you don’t ever really control how people see you, do you? Or even how you see yourself. Speaker_1: Exactly! And it's affected my fitness too, you know. I keep intending to start exercising properly again, but then… life gets in the way. Speaker_2: Tell me about it. I've been trying to get back into running, but I keep getting these really bad… (lowers voice) period cramps. It’s a nightmare. Absolutely debilitating. Speaker_1: Oh, I’m so sorry. Speaker_1: Right, so let’s run through this again. We’re looking at leveraging social media, but not in the way everyone else is doing it, right? No endless promotion of our own stuff. The entertainment value for me alone is worth the effort. Come on! Let's go! Hopefully, that captures the conversation style and context well! Let me know if you’d like any adjustments. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .H.H..

Speaker_1: (Sighs contentedly) Well, that was a feed, wasn’t it? Absolutely demolished that chicken. Speaker_3: It was lovely, Mark. Thanks for cooking. Speaker_1: Bye!H.HH.H.

Speaker_1: Right, so I’m thinking chicken and veg tonight. Simple, easy, and we need something relatively quick. This whole situation with the car is stressing me out. Speaker_2: Tell me about it. Are you both alright for sugar and milk with your tea? Speaker_3: Just a splash of milk for me, love. And a good strong brew. Speaker_4: Sugar, please. Two spoons. Now, anyone fancy a quick riddle while I’m waiting for the kettle to boil? Speaker_3: Oh, go on then. You know I can’t resist a good riddle. Speaker_4: Gets better every time you tell it, lass! Speaker_1: Alright then. What has an eye, but cannot see?H.HH.HH

Speaker_1: Right, so, pirates! Who wants to tell me what pirates *do*? Speaker_2: (Giggles) They say "Arrr!" and find treasure! Speaker_3: (Mumbling) They… they fight! Speaker_1: That’s right! They fight, and they sail the seas on big, scary ships looking for treasure. We're reading *Treasure Island* this week at school, remember? Do you want to draw some pirate ships, you two? Speaker_2: Yes! With lots of gold! And a parrot! Speaker_3: Can I draw a cannon? Speaker_1: Absolutely! Big cannons. Now, are you two hungry? I’m making cheese sandwiches. Speaker_2: Cheese! And then, the circus workshop! Remember? In a *real* circus ring! Speaker_2: With clowns! And acrobats! Speaker_1: Yes! We're learning to juggle and balance and do some simple magic tricks. Speaking of which, I think we need to practice our "abracadabra!" before we go. Speaker_3: (Shouts) Abracadabra! Speaker_2: Abracadabra! Make a carrot disappear! Speaker_1: (Laughing) Right, let’s not try *that* one just yet! We're also getting those Easter pictures back from school tomorrow, aren't we? I wonder what you drew, you two. Speaker_2: I drew a bunny! With lots and lots of chocolate eggs! Speaker_3: I drew a dragon breathing fire! Speaker_1: A dragon! That's brilliant.
